name: Healthcare and clinic
purpose: patient safety, infection control, medicines, consent, confidentiality, handovers, de-escalation, wellbeing of staff

identity.place: Ward 7 and the outpatients floor of a mid-sized district general hospital opened in 2009 on the edge of a temperate market town. A four-storey building of buff brick and vertical larch boarding wrapped around a full-height glazed 'hospital street' on the ground floor. Ward 7 on the second floor is a 28-bed adult medical ward: four-bed bays and single rooms on both sides of one long corridor, with the nurses' station in an open bay off the corridor halfway along it. The outpatients clinics and the outpatient pharmacy open off the hospital street on the ground floor. It is a well-kept, busy, ordinary hospital, not a television drama set.

identity.default_light: Late morning on a bright, slightly hazy day: soft daylight from the big windows on one side of each room, cool and gentle, with short, soft-edged sun patches only where a scene says so; every room also has its flat ceiling LED panels on, a neutral white that lights everything evenly from above, so shadows are soft and fall almost straight down under furniture. Corridors without windows are lit only by the ceiling panels.
identity.outside: Through the windows: the low roofs of a market town in slate and red tile, a line of trees along the hospital car park, a wooded hill on the horizon and a pale sky; no landmarks, no signs, no other hospital buildings close by.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one hospital (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the soft sage green wall, the pale blue-grey coved vinyl floor, a deep teal door frame, the pale oak handrail or a pale oak door with its tall vision panel, a white wall-mounted hand gel dispenser, the white lay-in ceiling grid with flat LED panels, a brushed stainless corner guard.
avoid: a television-drama hospital: blue-green gloom, flickering lights, dramatic shadows, rows of beeping screens
real brands, real hospital or health-service names and logos, readable signs, and any red cross or red crescent (protected emblems); medical symbols only as plain shapes with no words
people in the sets (the cast is separate); also no blood, wounds or anything frightening
a catalogue-clean hospital: every scene shows that care is happening here
anything blocking an escape route or a fire door: trolleys, wheelchairs and linen skips stand in alcoves or along a wall, never across a corridor
hand gel dispensers fixed right beside a sink (the sink has its own soap and paper towel dispensers); gel sits at bed feet, doorways and the points of care
unrealistic kit: oxygen cylinders lying loose, tubes hanging off nothing, a bed without castors or rails, a monitor floating with no stand or bracket
home furniture in clinical rooms: rugs, fabric sofas, wooden dining chairs; every surface here is wipe-clean

research: Real-world facts checked on 2026-10-15 (bed spaces 3.6 by 3.7 m: NHS Scotland NIPCM chapter 4 citing SHPN 04-01 and HBN 00-03; bed, overbed table, medicine trolley, basin, couch and medicine fridge sizes: makers' specification listings, sizes only; hand rub at the foot of the bed: Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care and a UK study; controlled drugs storage: NHS Scotland medicines policies; window restrictors: WHBN 00-10 Part D and the DH estates alert; handrails and corridor widths: HBN 00-04 summaries and the Dubai health facility guidelines; consulting room 16 m2: NHS Property Services room data; clean utility and treatment room areas: a Welsh hospital plan; nurses' station and counter heights: a hospital ergonomics standard and a UK building-control decision; pharmacy counter privacy: a Dutch controlled study and hospital pharmacy projects; hold-open fire doors: a university fire guidance note). Sources, the scene choice (D-156) and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-healthcare.md.
